facts.statement: Smilosuchus is an extinct genus of parasuchid phytosaurs that lived during the Late Triassic in North America.
facts.quote: Smilosuchus (from Ancient Greek σμίλη (smílē), meaning "knife, chisel", and Σοῦχος (Soûkhos), meaning "Sobek") is an extinct genus of leptosuchomorph parasuchid phytosaurs from the Late Triassic of North America.

facts.statement: Three species of Smilosuchus are known: S. gregorii, S. adamanensis, and S. lithodendrorum, all found in the Norian-aged Chinle Formation of Arizona.
facts.quote: Three species have been named: the type species S. gregorii, S. adamanensis, and S. lithodendrorum, all recovered from the Norian-aged Chinle Formation of Arizona.

facts.statement: Smilosuchus had an extremely large skull measuring up to 155 cm long, with total body length estimates varying up to 7 meters.
facts.quote: Its skull was extremely large, up to 155 cm long, although estimates for the overall length vary from 7 m

facts.statement: Smilosuchus possessed short, broad jaws with heterodont teeth, including large anterior tusks for impaling prey and blade-like teeth at the back for slicing flesh.
facts.quote: The jaws are very short and broad and the teeth are heterodont, with large tusks at the anterior of the mouth for impaling prey and more blade-like teeth for slicing flesh closer to the back of the mouth.

facts.statement: Smilosuchus had short and deep squamosal processes indicating a powerful bite, and its large size suggests it hunted large prey like Placerias.
facts.quote: Its squamosal processes are short and deep, indicating a powerful bite. This coupled with its large size (it is one of the largest known phytosaurs) suggests that it hunted large prey such as Placerias.

facts.statement: Some studies suggest that Smilosuchus might be congeneric with Leptosuchus, proposing that the enlarged rostral crest could have evolved independently in both genera.
facts.quote: Some studies seem to suggest that Smilosuchus is congeneric with Leptosuchus, as the enlarged crest could have been independently developed in Leptosuchus.

facts.statement: Smilosuchus lived from the Carnian to the Norian stages, approximately 237 to 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Norian (237 to 205.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: Like other phytosaurs, Smilosuchus had nostrils positioned close to the top of its head.
facts.quote: Like all phytosaurs, Smilosuchus had the nostrils close to the top of its head.

facts.statement: Smilosuchus possessed a larger rostral crest and nasal bulge supporting its raised nostrils compared to many other phytosaurs.
facts.quote: The rostral crest and nasal bulge supporting these raised nostrils was larger in Smilosuchus than in many other phytosaurs.
